components: A raw swap root commuting with a common order-six relabeling must pair its free antipodal orbits. Two six-cycles suffice for this symmetry; the old padded raw completion matches the logical fringe but fails the raw relabeling test.

Requiring transitive raw tag symmetry rather than a single relabeling gives a conditional minimum of thirteen; the affine example has a fixed point under the selected clock. If the clock is required to be free, a regular nonabelian example reaches 48.

Regular abelian translation covariance with an order-six element has additional half-element and inversion-root requirements; Z/12 times Z/4 supplies a size-48 witness. Commuting with the chosen frame is not required of arbitrary transitive symmetry.
candidates.declared_status: Finite raw-gate constructions and scoped symmetry size arguments. A logical fringe is not a raw symmetry measurement, and no empirical minimum of phase space is asserted.
missing_bridges: Motivate which raw symmetry, if any, applies to an independently observable physical carrier and test how the selected clock and any extra sheets transform.
Explain why the raw square-to-swap law and the required tags arise from physical interactions rather than merely being consistent finite constructions.

sources.text:
This is a finite resource question, not an assertion that the universe applies
this gate. On either homogeneous sector (two occupied or two empty cells)
let S be the tag alphabet, W(a,b)=(b,a), and demand T²=W on *all* raw pairs.
A successful logical fringe need not make T covariant. If naming a common
phase origin is pure convention, test the additional raw requirement
T(Ra,Rb)=(R,R)T(a,b) for an R of order six with an actual six-cycle.

The ordered antipodes (a,R³a) on each six-cycle form a free diagonal orbit
on which W is just R³. T commutes with W and R, so permutes these orbits.
A T-invariant one would require 2k=3 mod 6, impossible. They must pair;
one six-cycle plus up to five spare tags cannot work, irrespective of how R
permutes the spares. Two six-cycles suffice below. The extra sheet need not
be unobservable or exchangeable. No lattice or spacetime is presupposed.

Stronger optional symmetry: S is a finite abelian group K acting regularly
on itself by translations, including one of order six. A covariant T is
(a,a+d) -> (a+j(d), a+j(d)+t(d)). Hence t²(d)=-d and j(d)+j(t(d))=d.
If 2d=0, then t²(d)=d; comparing the last equation at d and t(d) forces
t(d)=d (commutativity is used), so d must have a half in K. The pairs
{d,-d} with d != -d must also occur in even number for inversion to have
a permutation square root. Conversely take a half for each involution and
interlace negative pairs in fours using the offsets below. These conditions
are sufficient, and the diagonal inputs can be fixed.

To obtain order six the odd part has size at least three. In the 2-primary
part every cyclic factor must have order divisible by four, otherwise its
order-two element has no half. With just one such factor, K has order 0
mod 4 and exactly two self-inverse elements: (|K|-2)/2 is odd. Therefore
at least two factors are needed, of total size at least 16. The size-48
example Z/12 x Z/4 attains the bound. This is NOT a claim about arbitrary
transitive/nonabelian actions, raw gates that do not square to W, or an
empirical minimal phase space. The algebraic argument is not a Lean proof.

def main() -> None:
    from scripts.probe_six_phase_exclusive_packet import t as old_coupler

    small = 0
    for twos, threes, ones in product(range(3), range(2), range(6)):
        lengths = (6, *((2,) * twos), *((3,) * threes), *((1,) * ones))
        if sum(lengths) >= 12:
            continue
        small += 1
        require(equivariant_root(rotation(lengths)) is None, "small alphabet escape")
    r = rotation((6, 6))
    gate = equivariant_root(r)
    if gate is None:
        raise ValueError("twelve-tag witness missing")
    check_raw(gate, [r])
    check_mixed(r, gate)
    # Original padding is sufficient for swap but at least one raw pair
    # witnesses failure of diagonal +1 on its operating tags with fixed spares.
    old_r = rotation((6, 1, 1))
    old_raw = {x: old_coupler(*x) for x in product(range(8), range(8))}
    mismatches = [
        x
        for x in sorted(old_raw)
        if old_raw[rotate(old_r, x)] != rotate(old_r, old_raw[x])
    ]
    require(bool(mismatches), "old raw completion unexpectedly origin free")
    # On the two same-sheet antipodal orbits a root exchanges sheets with
    # offsets s0,s1 summing to 3 mod 6; they cannot be equal. An occupancy
    # detector alone cannot notice any of these twelve raw discrepancies.
    sheet = tuple((i + 6) % 12 for i in range(12))
    antipodes = [(i, 6 * (i // 6) + (i + 3) % 6) for i in range(12)]
    require(
        all(gate[rotate(sheet, x)] != rotate(sheet, gate[x]) for x in antipodes),
        "unexpected additional raw sheet symmetry",
    )

For a finite tag set S, seek a map T on ordered pairs that squares to swap
and commutes with every simultaneous relabeling in a transitive group K.
A *chosen* R in K must have order six and an actual six-cycle. We do not
require K to commute with R: preserving a particular clock frame is stronger.
No geometry, particle interpretation, or physical update is derived here.

Lower bounds (elementary arguments, not a Lean artifact):

1. For C6 alone, every six-cycle supplies one free orbit of ordered antipodes
   on which swap acts by R^3. T preserves the union of those orbits since
   it commutes with R and swap and preserves period. On the orbit indices
   T induces an involution with no fixed index: a shift by j on a single
   six-cycle cannot square to the shift by three. Thus there are an even
   number of six-cycles and at least 12 tags.

2. For transitive K, if n=|S| is even then 16 divides n. To see this,
   suppose the 2-part v of n is 2, 4, or 8. For a Sylow 2-subgroup P of K
   all P-orbits have length at least v by orbit-stabilizer, and an odd
   number have length v (reduce their sum modulo 2v). Choose a P-stabilizer
   conjugacy type H with odd multiplicity k among these smallest orbits.
   In X=Fix_S(H) every P-point stabilizer is H itself (maximal possible
   order). Exactly the chosen k orbits contribute to X, with one regular
   W=N_P(H)/H orbit apiece. The normalizer condition in a finite p-group
   gives 1<|W|<=v. T restricts to a W-equivariant swap root on X^2.

   Write q=|W| and i=#elements w satisfying w^2=1. On X^2/W, swap has
   (q*k^2-i*k)/2 transpositions: only pairs (x,wx), w^2=1, in a single
   W-sheet contribute fixed orbits. A square permutation must be even.
   This excludes C4, C8, D8 (order eight), Q8 since k is odd and
   (q,i) is (4,2), (8,2), (8,6), (8,2), respectively.
   For C2, C2^2, C4xC2 and C2^3 choose a nonsquare involution a. T preserves
   the graph y=ax, characterized by swap(u)=a.u. On its k free W-orbits,
   T^2 acts by a, so its induced involution fixes at least one orbit. There
   T is a translation whose square must be a, impossible. These cases
   exhaust groups of orders 2, 4, 8. No census of larger groups is used.

Hence 13 is the absolute transitive minimum: the affine F13 construction
below attains it. If R is free (in particular if R is a regular translation)
then 6|n and therefore 48|n. A nonabelian regular example below attains 48.
If a transitive group must also preserve the chosen frame (commute with R),
all tags have the same R-period, hence six. These are finite model-selection
costs under supplied symmetry assumptions.

Regular criterion: in coordinates (x,xd), T=(x f(d),x f(d)p(d)), so
p^2(d)=d^-1 and f(d)f(p(d))=d. An even number of nontrivial inverse
pairs is necessary; pair them in fours (d,e,d^-1,e^-1), taking f values
(1,d,d^-1 e,e^-1). Involutions fixed by p need square roots; two paired
involutions d,e need a^-1 d a=e, then f takes values a,a^-1 d. Thus every
odd-size conjugacy class of involutions must be square-valued. Together
these conditions suffice (the identity may be fixed).
